thread:
pagerduty: PAGER — HIGH: 5xx/timeouts spike detected on runtime-gateway-prod. >60% 5xx across /generate and /chat over last 2m. correlation: batcher queue depth rising.

alex: seeing the same on our dashboards, batcher backlog jumping from ~300 to 7k in 90s. tail latency -> 30s, gateway 504s start at ~30s.

maria: I'm on call. quick sanity checks: any recent deploys to runtime-gateway or batcher?

josh: no prod deploys in last 6h. autoscaler events show no additional workers added — GPU pools pegged.

alex: logs:
```
2026-01-12T18:12:11Z runtime-gateway prod ERROR request handler: upstream timeout 504 path=/v1/generate model=redwood-compat-13b shards=2
2026-01-12T18:12:12Z batcher WARN enqueue latency=1200ms queue_depth=5120
2026-01-12T18:12:15Z batcher ERROR hol_block detected head_of_line_id=0x7f timeout=25s
```

ruth: customer impact: multiple mid-market customers reporting failed requests and degraded response times, reported error rate ~15-20% per region us-west-2. Need to estimate SLO/SLAs affected.

maria: priority: stop customer-facing errors ASAP. triage hypothesis: scheduler/batcher saturation causing head-of-line blocking -> gateways timing out. plan: 1) short-term reroute/gating 2) relieve batcher HOL 3) scale or evict backlog 4) longer-term fix.

josh: quick mitigation options: - enable model fallback to lighter variant (redwood-compat-7b) for non-critical requests - reduce max_batch_size to force smaller batches - enable immediate eviction of oldest requests - open extra gateway route to dedicated pool if available.

alex: can we temporarily throttle new low-priority traffic? we have a rate limit policy by customer tier. push a rule to gate free-tier and background jobs.

maria: on it. applying rate-limiter rule now: `POST /admin/rate-limits` payload -> `{"scope":"free-tier","limit":10rps}`. pushing.

infra-bot: action taken: rate-limit rule applied to scope=free-tier by maria.

josh: running `curl -s https://infra/api/batcher/evict?policy=hol&limit=1000 -X POST` to evict oldest 1k requests. this should break head-of-line chains.

alex: go ahead. I'm ready to monitor.

josh: done. response: `{"evicted":1000,"queue_now":6000}`. queue dip was tiny. maybe backlog deeper.

maria: start targeted reroute: set route policy for model=redwood-compat-13b -> fallback redwood-compat-7b for customers flagged as non-enterprise. pushing via runtime-routing.

alex: command: `./tools/routing/rebind --from=13b --to=7b --filter=customer_tier!=enterprise --duration=30m`

infra-bot: routing change queued by maria: rebind from 13b->7b for non-enterprise customers.

ruth: notify SRE and PLG about potential customer-visible degraded quality. we should create incident page and update status page.

maria: creating incident post now. status page: "Reduced availability for generation in us-west-2. Using fallback models for non-enterprise customers. Working on backlog eviction."

josh: telemetry: after evict and routing we see 5xx drop from 60%->22% in 2m, p95 latency down from 30s->9s, but queue still at ~5-6k. HOL signatures persist in specific queue shards: batcher-queue-14 and 17.

alex: suspect a stuck long-running request class: very long context/streaming sessions holding KV caches and blocking micro-batches. need to identify top offenders.

josh: running quick query to list top keys by token-length: `SELECT request_id, customer, seq_len FROM batcher_lease WHERE state='queued' ORDER BY seq_len DESC LIMIT 50` -> several >120k tokens, customers include customer-A, internal-backfill-job, customer-C.

maria: kill internal workflows and background backfills immediately. internal-backfill-job: @alex can you disable that job?

alex: disabling via scheduler UI -> `jobs/internal-backfill -> pause`. done. job paused.

josh: eviction attempt 2: `POST /api/batcher/evict?policy=aggressive&limit=5000` -> `{"evicted":4200,"queue_now":1800}`. big improvement.

ruth: nice. error rate now 5xx ~4%, still above normal but much better. we should keep fallback routing for a bit and monitor.

maria: putting a short-lived canary to re-enable enterprise traffic to 13b slowly to verify. policy: canary -> 10% enterprise traffic to primary.

alex: starting canary. `./tools/canary --route enterprise:13b --percent 10 --duration 15m`.

josh: monitoring traces: no regressions so far. canary healthy.

ruth: customer comms: draft a quick note for affected customers: "We're experiencing elevated error rates due to an internal traffic spike and batching saturation. We've rerouted non-enterprise traffic to a fallback model and evicted backlog to reduce errors. Enterprise customers are on a canary. We're continuing to monitor and will post updates." send?
maria: send now. posted to status and emailed affected customers list.

alex: next steps for mitigation/autorecovery: - add HOL detection alert to fire earlier at queue_depth>2k - implement automatic aggressive-evict when HOL signature detected - cap per-request token length enforced at ingress (reject >80k) - improve autoscaler to add workers on sustained queue growth.

josh: opened tickets: INF-1248 (auto-evict on hol), INF-1249 (per-request length cap), INF-1250 (autoscaler hysteresis tuning).

maria: handing off to night on-call @ruth for monitoring and follow ups. I'll stay reachable for questions.
ruth: taking over. monitoring dashboards pinned. will escalate to oncall-lead if metrics worsen.

infra-bot: summary: mitigation applied: rate-limits (free-tier), routing fallback (13b->7b non-enterprise), paused internal backfill, aggressive eviction -> queue reduced. 5xx from ~60% -> ~4% within 20m. next: follow-up tickets created and postmortem scheduled.

alex: thanks team. postmortem assignee: josh. include logs, timeline, impact CSV, and the commands we ran.

josh: acknowledged. starting the timeline doc now.

pagerduty: ALERT RESOLVED: 5xx spike mitigated.

maria: closing thread for now. update channel if we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
